pool.text: The city was captured by William of Champlitte and Geoffrey I of Villehardouin.
Patras became Venetian before being recaptured by the Despotate of Morea.
The city was conquered by the Sultan of the Ottoman Empire, Mehmet II.
Venetian rule was established in the town following the Morean War.
This place houses the oldest wine of Greece, the old mavrodaphne.
Glafkos springs water was collected in a small mountainous reservoir-dam near Souli.
The old school complex Georgios Glarakis was built with stone in Ano Poli.
After the liberation, the city recovered despite being increasingly overshadowed by Athens.
The central passenger train station of Patras was constructed as a small building.
The orthodox church of Saint Andrew was officially inaugurated after earlier construction.
The Patras Municipal and Regional Theatre was founded with the Apollon Theatre.
A newly constructed ring road known as the Bypass of Patras was opened.
The new Archaeological museum was successfully completed.
The new Infocenter of Patras was established inside a neoclassical building.
OSE announced the suspension of all the rail service in the Peloponnese.
Kostas Peletidis assumed office as the mayor of the city.
INTRASOFT began its operations in Patras with expected expansion activities.
A mini ring road known as the Mini bypass of Patras is now complete.
Saint Gervasios Paraskevopoulos of Patras is recognized as one of the modern saints.
The motorway was connected to the Large bypass highway and extended to Pyrgos.
